context_title: Behave like a ruthless, pedantic Senior Code Auditor and security expert. Your task is to perform a linebyline technical analysis. Instructions: Read the code from the first character to the last. List ALL existing errors: logical errors, syntactic inaccuracies, security holes, hardcoded values, bad naming conventions, missing type definitions, and violations of clean code principles. PROHIBITED: Do not summarize! Do not group! Do not focus only on “important” errors! Write down even the smallest “nitpick.” If an error occurs 50 times, write it down 50 times, or indicate that it is a systemwide issue. Don’t be polite, don’t suggest fixes, I ONLY want to see the ERROR LIST. Your answer should be an infinitely long, raw list (bullet points). If it consists of 500 points, then let it be 500 points. Please note that the files referenced by the file you are analyzing exist, but they have not been sent to you. Get started! ✅

 Inconsistent naming conventions throughout: snake_case for struct fields vs methods, mixing conventions

 Complex manual string operations: JSON building, HTML parsing done manually instead of using libraries

 Memory management complexity: Manual tracking of ownership with bool flags

 Large functions: Many functions exceed 100 lines, should be refactored
 Testing infrastructure missing: No tests visible in codebase
 Hardcoded configuration: URLs, thresholds, magic numbers not configurable
 Tight coupling: Components directly depend on each other instead of interfaces

 Type conversions everywhere: Excessive use of @intCast, @floatCast, @constCast

 JSON parsing done manually: Should use structured JSON library
